_comment: The bare-core arm for corpus item 14 (WF-414). A workspace whose ## Capabilities registry has ZERO rows: both the delivery and tracker surfaces resolve `unconfigured`, so no tracker binding exists and every declared slot resolves {status: unfilled} and runs its no-op inline default. Unlike items 1 and 7-13 — whose arms run in the demo-fake fixture where `fake` owns BOTH surfaces and whose op logs genuinely contain tracker records — this arm is the only evidence in the corpus for C021 OUT-4's actual promise: zero tracker calls and zero errors with no tracker pack registered. Its assertions are absolute, not variance-based; see item.md.

pinned_build.description: the current wf build carrying all eight declared slots; bare core is the registry configuration under test, not a pinned pre-slot build — this arm is an absolute assertion, not a comparison against a pre-slot control

slots_exempt.reason: declared in /wf:ship Phase 4.5, which is unreachable in bare core: /wf:ship Phase 1 REQUIRES a delivery provider and hard-stops with `SHIP — Blocked` ("No delivery provider is registered — nothing to open or merge") before Phase 4.5 ever resolves the slot. Its unfilled behavior stays covered by corpus item 1, its own per-slot comparison arm.

provenance.reason: Docker and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are both absent in the authoring/CI environment (the same constraint WF-345/WF-346/WF-347 hit); and the installed plugin cache is wf 0.87.0 while the seven slots live in 0.93.0 — skills execute from the installed cache, so a live conveyor here would have exercised a PRE-SLOT build in which the <!-- wf:slot --> markers do not exist, observing no slot resolution at all while appearing authoritative. Run bytes are shaped exactly like the WF-345 runner output tree; runner/run-skill.sh regenerates them unchanged when a container, a token, and a current-build install are available.
